summaries.subject: Observational Analysis of Unusual X-Band Radar Reflections in the Gulf of Maine
summaries.executive_summary: Coastal radar stations NEXRAD KCBW and KGYX detected non-precipitating echoes exceeding 450 m/s with localized NOAA-21 sea-surface temperature anomalies of +1.8 K.

claims.statement: Radar stations KCBW and KGYX detected anomalous non-precipitating echoes with radial velocities over 450 m/s on 2026-08-12.

citations.verbatim_passage: On 2026-08-12 between 03:14 UTC and 04:22 UTC, coastal meteorological radar stations NEXRAD KCBW and KGYX registered anomalous non-precipitating echoes exhibiting radial velocities exceeding 450 meters per second.

claims.statement: Target echo Charlie-1 registered an apparent velocity of 482 m/s (+/- 15 m/s) at 3,200 meters altitude.

citations.verbatim_passage: At 03:22:15 UTC, target echo Charlie-1 exhibited an apparent velocity of 482 m/s (+/- 15 m/s) at an altitude of 3,200 meters above mean sea level.

claims.statement: Radar cross-section peaked at 42.5 dBZ with differential reflectivity (ZDR) of -1.4 dB, inconsistent with standard biological or hydrometeor scatterers.

citations.verbatim_passage: At 03:41:00 UTC, the radar cross-section spiked to 42.5 dBZ with a differential reflectivity (ZDR) of -1.4 dB, inconsistent with standard biological or hydrometeor scatterers.

summaries.declared_methodology: Dual-polarization Doppler radar in VCP 212 normalized against 30-day sea-clutter baselines and Portland Jetport thermal inversion soundings.
stated_limitations: Refraction effects from the atmospheric ducting inversion layer could not be completely decoupled from kinetic motion.
Secondary multipath reflections from sea-surface chop introduce range uncertainty up to 1,200 meters.
Ground-truth optical corroboration was precluded by overcast cloud ceilings below 1,000 meters.
unresolved_questions: Did the thermal sea-surface anomaly precede or follow the passage of the primary radar return?
What physical mechanism accounts for the negative differential reflectivity (-1.4 dB) in the absence of frozen hydrometeors?
Were maritime Automatic Identification System (AIS) vessel transponders subjected to localized radio-frequency interference during the event interval?

summaries.subject: Declassified Record Extract (Partial Scan)
summaries.executive_summary: Partial flight safety extract noting radio direction finder deviations on airway J-75 on 2026-08-12; page 2 unreadable due to severe optical toner corruption.

claims.statement: Three commercial airliners on airway J-75 noted radio direction finder deviations at 03:30 UTC on 2026-08-12.

citations.verbatim_passage: The preliminary flight safety report indicates that three commercial airliners on airway J-75 noted anomalous radio direction finder deviations on 2026-08-12 at 03:30 UTC.

claims.statement: Aircraft compasses stabilized immediately upon crossing waypoint PEARS.

citations.verbatim_passage: Aircraft flight crews reported that navigational compasses stabilized immediately upon crossing waypoint PEARS.

summaries.declared_methodology: Air traffic control record review and pilot debrief.
stated_limitations: Page 2 suffered complete optical corruption and could not be recovered by OCR.
unresolved_questions: What occurred between the initial deviation at 03:30 UTC and stabilization at waypoint PEARS?
